marta (product): Quick check-in: drafting the Private Deployment onboarding playbook for VPC/on-prem. Goal: decide three shipping lanes (Lean, Practical, Enterprise) with concrete launch gates. Emphasis: customer-managed networking, upgrade strategies (in-place vs blue/green), and packaging (helm/operator/airgap VM). Drop concrete acceptance criteria and any non-negotiable blockers.

juan (eng-platform): Agree. From platform POV, biggest unknowns are state transfer for model KV caches during blue/green and image size limits for airgapped VM images. Need to pick a model size target (e.g., up to 13B quantized) to scope disk and RAM.

mei (solutions): Field perspective: customers always want the same outbound IPs and stable DNS records. Also they want a pre-approved maintenance window and a rollback playbook that they can sign off on. Some will insist on no external callbacks at all.

raj (security): Security must be explicit: list of allowed telemetry endpoints, cert pinning for control plane, and HSM/KMS connectivity patterns. For blue/green, we need a signed attestation that new instances have the same model checksum.

marta (product): Okay — propose 3 lanes with short acceptance bullets. Lean, Practical, Enterprise.

juan (eng-platform): Lean lane (fastest): Helm chart + operator optional, uses our nat-relay, assumes customer can accept transient egress change. Acceptance: helm deploy completes with default values in <20min; exposed endpoints serve traffic; basic health + logs available via local endpoint; document rollback steps.

juan (eng-platform): Practical lane (recommended): Operator with egress pinning, DNS preservation tool that migrates CNAMEs, and rolling upgrades with KV cache warmup. Acceptance: operator supports `egressPin` and `dnsPreserve` flags; rolling upgrade with staged replica replacement preserving p95 within 10% baseline; documented preflight verifies BGP/peering or NAT behavior.

mei (solutions): Enterprise lane: airgapped VM/OCI image bundle, signed manifests, HSM-backed KMS integration, and control-plane-optional install (admin chooses offline control-plane). Acceptance: signed offline bundle verified in lab; KMS via customer gateway tested (encrypt/decrypt), and upgrade path supports blue/green with model checksum attestation and <30m maintenance window.

raj (security): Add to Enterprise acceptance: ability to run without any outbound egress and local-only telemetry sink. Also require audit logs retained for 90 days and a documented key rotation procedure.

marta (product): Great. Launch gates? What's required before we call a lane GA?

mei (solutions): Lean: 2 internal pilots + docs. Practical: 3 customer pilots across distinct network setups (NAT, public IP, direct peering). Enterprise: 1 paid enterprise pilot + security signoff + signed-bundle CI green.

juan (eng-platform): Engineering risks: 1) KV cache cold-start causing unacceptable tail latency during rolling upgrades. 2) Airgap bundle signing and reproducible builds hitting edgecases. 3) BGP/peering matrix—too many topologies to test exhaustively.

raj (security): Operational risk: customers refusing any connectivity prevents our health/metrics. Mitigation: provide a local metrics aggregator and a secure, customer-controlled upload path (SFTP/S3 gateway) if allowed.

mei (solutions): Sales risk: multi-week netops cycles. Mitigation: provide a short "NetOps checklist" and an optional paid NetOps concierge to fast-track onboarding.

marta (product): Can someone draft a one-page preflight checklist we can hand to SEs? Keep it under 8 items.

juan (eng-platform): Draft checklist:
- Confirm desired shipping lane (Lean / Practical / Enterprise)
- Egress behavior: public IPs, NAT, or BGP peering (provide example IPs/CIDRs)
- Confirm DNS ownership and migrator permissions (if dnsPreserve needed)
- KMS/HSM endpoint + auth method (for Enterprise)
- Disk and GPU capacity on nodes (min disk 100GB for Practical+, GPU driver versions)
- Time sync (NTP/chrony) and firewall rules for required ports
- If airgapped: provide signed bundle transfer method and bootstrap token

mei (solutions): I'll add an implementation timeline for customers: 2 weeks prep (netops + approvals), 3-7 days install, 2-6 weeks validation depending on traffic.

raj (security): Note: for regulatory customers require offline attestations and yearly pen-test; add that to the Enterprise contract checklist.

ci-bot: nightly-priv-bundle build 2026-03-22 status: FAILURE at `repro-sign` step. See https://ci.redwood/ins/priv-bundle/20260322 :warning:

juan (eng-platform): That CI failure blocks Enterprise lane demos. I'll triage the reproducible-build issue tomorrow.

marta (product): Owners: Juan = platform/engineering for all lanes. Mei = field pilots and SE collateral. Raj = security signoffs and Enterprise checklist. Next actions: 1) convert this thread to a short playbook doc. 2) run a test install for Lean in our lab this week. 3) schedule pilot outreach for Practical lane.

mei (solutions): I'll pause Enterprise outbound until the `repro-sign` CI issue is fixed.

marta (product): Thanks everyone — will capture decisions and add cards to the roadmap board. :white_check_mark:
